chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A man has estates, some of them near to one another, and he goes out and circulates among them—should he perform the prayer in full or shorten it? He said: He should perform it in full.

So there is nothing in this report that contradicts what we have stated earlier, because it does not mention the distance he travels therein. If that is not mentioned in it, it remains possible that what is meant is when the estate is near to him; in that case, shortening does not become obligatory upon him.

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: shortening of the prayer during travel
key_terms.فَيَطُوفُ: he goes around or circulates among them
key_terms.مِقْدَارِ الْمَسَافَةِ: the extent of the travel distance
key_terms.يُتِمُّ: he performs the prayer in full

ai.seo_question: If a person travels between nearby estates, should he shorten salat (prayer) or perform it in full?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of salat (prayer) for a person traveling among nearby estates. The Imam عليه السلام rules that he should perform the prayer in full, and the compiler clarifies that this does not conflict with prior rulings because the travel distance is unspecified and may be too short to require shortening.
